title: Habib Goes Back-to-Back: Habibsters Run Away With Buckaroo Bowl II
dek: Kaushal bulldozed the 2024 season at 11-3 and won a second straight title, Brucie crashed the Bowl at .500, and Sonny's Ben Dover held onto the basement key for another year.
body: Two seasons, two Buckaroo Bowls, one name on both trophies. Kaushal's Habibsters went 11-3, earned the No. 1 seed, and then won two playoff rounds by a combined 167 points to claim Buckaroo Bowl II. Habib wasn't just the best team in 2024. He was the guy doing 90 in the left lane while the rest of the league was still checking its mirrors, and this time nobody could pull him over.

The season opened with a warning shot from the most unlikely place. Ramon's Araleasers posted 166.58 points in Week 1, the highest single-week score of the year, and for one glorious weekend Brucie looked like a man who had figured fantasy football out. The rest of his regular season was a coin flip, a perfectly balanced 7-7, but that opening blast was a preview of what he could do when it counted.

The real regular-season puzzle belonged to Randy. The fumblers scored 1,595.1 points, the most in the league by a wide margin, and only had an 8-6 record and the No. 2 seed to show for it. He also took part in exactly as many trades as everyone else: zero. Not one trade was made in the Buckaroo Football League all season, which means Randy spent the year complaining about his roster, refusing every offer, and setting the league's scoring record anyway. Honestly, he may have been right not to trade.

At the other end, Sonny's Ben Dover finished 5-9 with a league-low 1,304.3 points, capped by a Week 12 performance of 44.1 points, the lowest score of the year. That is a stat line that makes a commissioner wonder if he can quietly edit the scoring settings. Mekhi's Dawgs also finished 5-9 but outscored Ben Dover by more than 100 points, so the waiver-wire king escaped the cellar and Sonny claimed last place for the second year in a row. Nobody watching that 44-point Sunday would have believed the worst-to-first story still to come.

The playoffs ran on two-week totals, and the semifinals split right down the middle. Habibsters handled Alan's Team Pillbert 296.96 to 245.08, which ended the villain's run despite Philliberto squeezing into the field at 6-8 as the No. 4 seed. In the other bracket, the regular-season points king fell: Ramon's Araleasers beat The fumblers 202.44 to 176.14. All those points, no trades, and Randy got knocked out by the turncoat Bills fan. You can imagine the complaints.

Buckaroo Bowl II was not close. Habibsters beat Araleasers 261.44 to 145.28 over two weeks, a 116-point margin that was less a championship game than a victory lap. Brucie's run from the 3 seed to the title game was a real accomplishment, but it ran straight into the same buzz saw that had been flattening the league since September. Alan settled for third, Randy for fourth, and the Dawgs for fifth.

So Kaushal leaves 2024 with two rings and the league leaves it with questions. Can anyone stop Habib? Will Randy ever trade? Can Sonny's team find the bottom of the standings? Buckaroo Bowl III is on the clock, and for now the throne still belongs to the Habibsters.
